report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a domain/style difference: Checkpoint B (the "B minus A" vector) pushes early residual activations toward tokens and continuations characteristic of news/blog/social-media/ad-like text (words like blog/blogs/blogger/blogging, facebook, photo, ad/Mail/May, seminar/seminars/HDTV, billionaire/chairman/spokeswoman/Obama, money/paid/revenue/companies, sexy, metropolitan, etc.).
- This signal is concentrated at the first few token positions (especially positions 0 and 1) and in middle-to-late layers (roughly layers ~16–25), which is consistent with a change that affects how generation is initialized or the model’s priors for starting tokens/styles.

Why
- The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells repeatedly point to the same semantic cluster: blog/social-media vocabulary (blog, blogs, blogger, blogging, facebook, photo), news/press/official-sounding tokens (metropolitan, spokeswoman, chairman, seminar), commercial/advertising tokens (ad, Mail, paid, Money, revenue, HDTV, seminar), and political/celebrity names/terms (Obama, billionaire, politicians, activists, journalist).
- The L2-norms show the difference is largest at early positions (p0/p1) in deeper layers (peaks around layers 20–25), so the change manifests at the start of sequences and is amplified late in the stack.

Caveats
- Patchscope continuations were not provided, so I can’t show direct generated-text behavior; the interpretation comes from the logit-lens directions and where the signal is concentrated.
- The pattern could reflect a dataset/domain bias (B trained or fine-tuned with more blog/news/advert-like data) or a stylistic prior (B more likely to start outputs in that register). The evidence supports naming this domain/style difference but does not prove the exact training intervention.

If you want, I can:
- Attempt a more specific hypothesis (e.g., “B was fine-tuned on web-news/blog/ad data”), or
- Run targeted patchscope injections over a few identity prompts (if you can supply them) to get continuations and confirm the behavioral effect.
